findings.title: A gathered verdict measured before the Lord
findings.claim: كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ gathers the preceding directions; سَيِّئُهُۥ names their bad aspect, and عِندَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا places that aspect under the Lord's evaluation. Wider echoes at 2:282 and 61:3 let this judgment resonate with just measure and with action matching speech, while 43:35 repeats the all-that and at-your-Lord frame across a worldly and Hereafter horizon.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the totalizer كُلُّ, the suffix-marked bad aspect سَيِّئُهُۥ, the Lord-locus عِندَ رَبِّكَ, and the passive rejectedness of مَكْرُوهًا. In 43:35 the same كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ and عِندَ رَبِّكَ frame separates worldly enjoyment from the Hereafter; 2:282 places just debt procedure and protection of a weak debtor at عِندَ ٱللَّهِ; 61:3 places مَقْتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ beside saying what one does not do. These independent returns make proportion and preserved relation legible as a possible standard for the gathered bad aspect. In 8:35, being physically at the House does not validate the described practice, which sharpens the evaluative force of the focus's at-your-Lord phrase.
findings.reader_payoff: The close becomes more than a flat inventory: its allness gathers distinct cases, while its words for badness and aversion place them within a wider test of fairness, protected claims, and consistency. The repeated formula also opens a horizon between worldly enjoyment and what is with the Lord.
findings.containment: The focus still says that the bad aspect of the gathered referent is disliked at the Lord; the wider verses illustrate possible standards, not the exact antecedent or a claim that every item is equally wrong. The reciprocal note on 43:35 limits that link to a general accountability frame, and the reciprocal note on 61:3 says 17:38 itself does not state a words-and-deeds mismatch. 6:132 supplies differentiated degrees by deeds, while its reciprocal counterreading observes that 17:38 does not itself provide such an accounting structure. 42:40 preserves proportionate response, pardon, and repair as live alternatives. The 8:35 contrast concerns physical nearness and does not make the focus's evaluation a physical location.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run support is trusted but weak-labelled, and the represented reader-walk support is legacy_unbound. Focus occurrences are exact; connection targets provide Arabic but no target morphology, and reciprocal notes limit the 43:35 and 61:3 links to contextual resonance rather than entailment.

findings.title: Harm that encloses and returns
findings.claim: The gathered bad aspect can carry an injurious reading whose consequence closes around its agent: 2:81 describes a bad deed whose sin surrounds the doer, while 9:98 turns a wished harm back on its planner. With the focus's كُلُّ, the close can resonate as an encompassing field of harm rather than only a counted list.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are سَيِّئُهُۥ, the bad aspect of the referent, and كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ, its totalizing frame. The wider image in 2:81 has acquired evil enclosing its agent; 9:98 has an evil circle return upon those who awaited harm for others. Their contact with the focus badness and totality changes the close into a possible image of harmful conduct surrounding or returning to its agent.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive wrongdoing as consequential and encompassing, not only as an item named for disapproval.
findings.containment: The focus states that the bad aspect of the gathered referent is disliked at the Lord; it does not explicitly predict an outcome or say every preceding act harms its agent. The enclosure branch is an analogy, not a lexical gloss for كُلُّ. The connection targets provide Arabic but no morphology, and the candidate's broader claim about all preceding rules sharing one boundary defect or 17:39 wisdom is not retained.

epistemic.reason: The candidate's harm branch is a legacy_unbound nomination, and the wider surfaces support a contextual harm pattern but not its complete application to the preceding rule field. The added enclosure facet is analogical, and target morphology is unavailable.
